source_field_sets.expect: Read pp. 653–655 and 668–671 in a PDF of the journal pages hosted by a website (file Capital.pdf; running heads 'Public Culture', folios 653–678, printer's date 11/16/00). OpenAlex W2067418547 and the DOI agree (Public Culture 12:3, pp. 653–678). The first-page note says 'A slightly different version of this essay, entitled “The Two Histories of Capital,” constitutes a chapter in my book Provincializing Europe' (p. 653). Passages used: History 1 and History 2 as pasts 'posited by capital' and pasts outside capital's 'life-process' (p. 655); 'Let us call this history ... History 1. Marx opposes to History 1 another kind of past that we will call History 2' (p. 668); History 2's 'are thus not pasts separate from capital; they are pasts that inhere in capital and yet interrupt and punctuate the run of capital’s own logic' (p. 670); the historicist 'not yet' and 'history as a waiting room' (p. 670); History 2 as 'a category charged with the negative function of constantly interrupting the totalizing thrusts of History 1' (p. 671). Chapter 2 of the book itself was not read; the essay is cited as his 2000 statement, not as the book's text.
